prompt: Hand-drawn paper map of the Bay of Cadiz and the Atlantic coast of Andalusia, old pen-and-ink nautical chart, landscape ~3:2. Aged off-white paper with fold creases, vermillion ink coastline, flat deep blue-teal sea, plain land with thin ink roads and two rivers. Geography drawn precisely: the Bay of Cadiz opening westward; CADIZ at the tip of the long narrow spit forming the southern arm; ROTA directly across the bay on the NORTHWESTERN headland, facing Cadiz across the bay mouth; EL PUERTO DE SANTA MARIA inside the bay east of Rota at the Guadalete mouth; JEREZ DE LA FRONTERA inland to the northeast; the wider Guadalquivir mouth further north, drawn but UNLABELLED; GIBRALTAR far southeast as a rocky promontory. Five ink circles with small neat hand-lettered capitals, no other place names. Thin uneven vermillion route line connecting them. Two widely letterspaced area labels in lighter ink: OCEANO ATLANTICO over the open sea lower left, ANDALUCIA inland upper right. Compass rose lower left over the sea: classic nautical wind rose in fine ink linework, 16-pointed star with long and short rays, graduated degree ring with fine ticks, northern point filled warm dark gold. NOTHING ELSE: no scale bar, legend, cartouche, border, photographs or modern pins; absolutely not a digital map. Palette: aged paper off-white, one deep blue-teal, one muted vermillion, warm dark gold for the north point only, near-black lettering.
note: Zweite Fassung. Die erste zeichnete ROTA an die Guadalquivir-Muendung, wo Sanlucar de Barrameda liegt — rund 10 km daneben (Befund Henning 20.09.). Jetzt liegt Rota korrekt an der Nordwestspitze der Bucht, gegenueber Cadiz. Kompassrose nach dem Vorbild des VuZ-Designsystems (nautische Windrose, goldener Nordpfeil). Gezeichnete Karte, kein Kartendienst.
